summary.text: The geodynamo is the process in which liquid iron convecting in Earth's outer core induces and constantly maintains the planet's magnetic field.
Dynamo theory says a fluid that rotates, convects and conducts electricity can keep a magnetic field going over astronomical timescales.
Without convection the field would decay, and Earth's rotation, through the Coriolis effect, organizes the flow into columns lined up with the spin axis.

facts.label: Conducting fluid
facts.value: Liquid iron in the outer core

facts.label: Decay without convection
facts.value: Dipole field gone in about 20,000 years

items.prompt: In 1600 William Gilbert concluded that Earth is magnetic. What did he think was the cause?

options.label: Electric currents deep inside
Light streaming from the Sun
Swirling liquid iron in the core
Permanent magnetism like lodestone

items.explain: Gilbert's hypothesis was permanent magnetism, such as that found in lodestone; internal currents and the dynamo came later.

items.prompt: Why must Earth's outer core keep convecting for the magnetic field to last?

options.label: Without it the field would decay away
Without it the field would flip daily
Without it the core would turn to rock
Without it the Sun's field would take over

items.explain: To hold the field against ohmic decay, which would remove the dipole field in about 20,000 years, the outer core must be convecting.

items.prompt: Jupiter's moon Io gets enough tidal heating to melt its inner core, yet may have no dynamo. Why?

options.label: It spins far too quickly
Its interior can't conduct electricity
It sits too far from the Sun
Its core is too hot to move

items.explain: A dynamo needs a liquid interior that conducts electricity; Io and Enceladus may lack one because they cannot conduct electricity.

items.prompt: Mercury is a small planet, yet it has a magnetic field. What explains this?

options.label: Its crust is made of lodestone
The Sun's field magnetizes it
A conductive liquid iron core
Its very fast spin alone

items.explain: Mercury has a conductive liquid core, created by its iron composition and by friction from its highly elliptical orbit.

items.prompt: What part does Earth's rotation play in the geodynamo?

options.label: It cools the core so the iron can flow
It makes electricity directly by rubbing
It lines up flows and currents into columns
None; the field would be the same without it

items.explain: Rotation supplies the Coriolis effect, which organizes fluid motions and electric currents into columns aligned with the rotation axis.

items.prompt: In a dynamo model, the flow sits below the critical magnetic Reynolds number. What happens to a magnetic field imposed on it?

options.label: It grows stronger over time
It dies away
It stays exactly as it was
It flips back and forth

items.explain: Above the critical magnetic Reynolds number the flow amplifies the field; below it, the field dissipates.
